cycles.title: Genesis — convert the repository into a reproducible proof-search laboratory
cycles.objective: Create a machine-readable laboratory that preserves historical experiments while admitting only formal, falsifiable, independently reproducible complexity hypotheses.
actions: Rewrote README.md around falsification and independent reproduction.
Created a registry schema and validation contract.
Moved six vague, circular, or destroyed routes into the permanent graveyard.
Added a deterministic registry validator and continuous-integration gate.
discoveries: The current survivors can be organized as exact polynomial lifts into tractable mathematical classes.
The principal unresolved question is not whether the target class is tractable, but whether every CNF admits the promised uniform polynomial-size exact lift.
Direct-encoding lower bounds must not be overstated as lower bounds against unrestricted polynomial auxiliary-variable lifts.
cycles.claim_boundary: No hypothesis advanced beyond UNDER_ATTACK. No novelty claim, algorithmic breakthrough, or P-versus-NP proof was produced.
next_cycle: Perform a literature and lower-bound audit for each exact lift class.
Define restricted transformation models that are strong enough to be useful but narrow enough to attack rigorously.
Implement small-instance synthesis to search for minimal counterexamples to restricted versions.
Require external reproduction before any computational observation is promoted beyond R3.

cycles.title: Survivor frontiers — remove circular lift value and register audited open boundaries
cycles.objective: Find hypotheses that survive a bounded self-refutation attempt, distinguish literature frontiers from JANUS-generated mechanisms, and prevent unrestricted solve-and-encode conjectures from masquerading as independent progress.
actions: Audited H001-H004 for equivalence to P = NP through the solve-and-encode construction.
Marked H001-H004 as weakened in research value without falsely declaring their exact statements destroyed.
Added a primary-source references registry and machine validation of literature cross-references.
Registered four current proof-complexity lower-bound frontiers H005-H008.
Registered two restricted JANUS algorithmic mechanisms H009-H010 that syntactically block an unrestricted SAT oracle.
Registered the opposing Extended Frege polynomial-boundedness frontier H011.
Recorded eighteen new attacks A009-A026 and five new observations O006-O010.
discoveries: H001-H004 are theorem-equivalent to P = NP as stated because their unrestricted polynomial-time transformers may solve the instance before emitting a trivial target object.
The registry must separate external open frontiers from JANUS-generated conjectures and must never imply novelty from inclusion.
Restricted proof-system progress in 2024-2026 leaves several stronger unrestricted lower-bound questions open.
Mutually exclusive hypotheses can both survive the current attacks; OPEN is a bookkeeping state, not a belief score.
H009 and H010 are the first JANUS algorithmic descendants whose allowed operations are restricted independently of a general SAT solver.
cycles.claim_boundary: No new theorem, algorithm, proof lower bound, or resolution of P versus NP was produced. The literature audit is bounded to the cited primary sources and can be revised when new work appears.
next_cycle: Formalize H009 as a concrete finite rewrite grammar and search for separator-preservation counterexamples on expander and Tseitin families.
Formalize H010 in a small proof checker and test whether known polynomial-calculus hard instances remain hard after the allowed extension rules.
Choose explicit candidate families for H005-H008 rather than leaving them as frontier existential statements.
Add automated freshness review dates to literature-frontier entries.
Seek independent mathematical review of the exact quantifiers and proof-system definitions.
